A deep grinding sound heralds the peaceful packs of khanaur as they chew through stalks of tall grass and dig up tubers to feed their 
voracious appetites. Roaming in groups of several individuals, their larvae stuck on the undersides of the adult members to keep their 
familial packs tight and moving, the khanaur travel the Farplains in slow seasonal migrations. Grazing in close proximity to each other 
to ward off any nearby predators, while the larger females of their group patrol, their massive forelimbs stomping into the soil to warn 
any that think they can attempt to penetrate their heavily armored chitin shells. Keeping pace with their roaming herd are packs of 
khanith, picking off smaller predators that would otherwise prey on the larvae grubs, their presence welcomed by their larger cousins.

Encountering Th ese large herbivores look deceptively docile 
when slowly grazing in the fi elds, their eyes staring vacantly 
as they chew, but they are always watching for danger. Once 
confronted by aggressive creatures they quickly form a defensive 
posture, their instinctual need to protect taking over. If roused 
to violence, there is little that would calm them until the hostile 
is long gone or crushed into the soil.
